model_output:
The Ramayana is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Mahabharata. It tells the story of Rama, an avatar (divine incarnation) of the god Vishnu, who was born to king Dasaratha of Ayodhya.
The story begins with the sage Visvamitra demanding that King Dasaratha give him his daughter Princess Seeta in marriage. When Dasaratha refuses, Visvamitra performs a series of miracles to prove his spiritual power, and eventually Dasaratha agrees to the marriage. However, Visvamitra then demands that Seeta be sent to his forest hermitage, and when Dasaratha agrees to this as well, he sends Rama, his own son, to accompany Seeta to the hermitage.
In the hermitage, Seeta is abducted by the demon king Ravana, who has been lusting after her. Rama and his brother Lakshmana set out to rescue Seeta, and they are aided by a monkey king named Hanuman and a whole army of monkeys. After a long search, they finally find Seeta and defeat Ravana in a great battle.
After the victory, Rama and Seeta return to Ayodhya, where Rama is crowned king. However, the story does not end there, as Rama's reign is not without problems. He has to face challenges from his own brothers and his own wife, and eventually he has to leave the palace and go into exile for 14 years. The story ends with Rama returning to Ayodhya and reclaiming his rightful place as king.
The Ramayana is a complex and multilayered story that explores themes of love, duty, loyalty, and the struggle between good and evil. It is considered one of the greatest works of Indian literature and has had a profound influence on Indian culture and religion.
